NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks condenser overall heat transfer coefficient (U-value) or terminal temperature difference (TTD) as direct measures of heat transfer performance. My observable is the *cross-sectional flow non-uniformity index* calculated from temperature measurements across the tube bundle, which detects the onset of localized biofouling before it significantly impacts overall heat transfer. This departure is genuine because localized flow restriction creates temperature patterns that precede measurable changes in bulk performance metrics, as fouling first creates preferential flow paths that skew temperature distribution before reducing overall heat transfer capacity.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is Fourier's law of heat conduction and conservation of energy: Q = m·cp·ΔT = U·A·LMTD. As biofouling accumulates locally, flow resistance increases, causing velocity reduction in affected tubes. This reduces local heat transfer, creating measurable temperature differences across the tube bundle. The magnitude verification: A 10% flow reduction in a tube section would cause approximately a 2-3°C temperature rise at that location (based on typical condenser conditions with ΔT ≈ 10-15°C), detectable before overall U-value changes by 3-5%.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) Existing condenser steam inlet temperature sensors (already installed), 2) Existing condensate outlet temperature sensors (already installed), 3) Data acquisition system (already installed), 4) Processing algorithm (standard engineering computation). Materials: None required beyond existing infrastructure. Instruments: No additional hardware required. Procedure: 1) Collect temperature measurements from multiple points across condenser tube bundle (existing sensors), 2) Calculate temperature variance across measurement points, 3) Compare against baseline clean condition, 4) Apply flow non-uniformity index calculation: σ(T)/T_avg, where σ(T) is standard deviation of temperatures and T_avg is mean temperature. Algorithm requires development but uses standard statistical methods.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: SAME, uses existing sensors. Operability: SAME, processing runs in background. Maintenance: SAME, no additional maintenance requirements. Cost class: SAME, only software development cost (minimal compared to hardware). The approach has same deployment burden as standard monitoring but provides earlier detection by leveraging existing measurements in a novel way. No additional hardware or infrastructure costs.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: 1) Establish baseline temperature distribution across condenser tube bundle during clean operation, 2) Calculate initial flow non-uniformity index (σ(T)/T_avg), 3) Monitor temperature distribution weekly, 4) Calculate index continuously, 5) Compare against threshold. Instruments: Existing temperature sensors and data acquisition system. Pass threshold: Index increases by 20% above baseline. Duration: 3-month monitoring period. Kill criterion: If index does not consistently increase 20% before back-pressure reaches derating limit in at least 3 historical cases or during accelerated fouling test, the predictor is falsified.
